volume: 第十卷貪窶部 Volume 10: Greedy Lusts Department

stories.text: 一富人酷嗜古董，而不辨真假。或偽以虞舜所造漆碗。周公撻伯禽之杖，與孔子杏壇所坐之席求售，各以千金得之。囊資既空，乃左執虞舜之碗，右持周公之杖，身披孔子之席，而行乞于市，曰：「求賜太公九府錢一文。」
stories.translation: A wealthy man was extremely fond of antiques, but could not distinguish between genuine and fake ones. Someone presented a lacquered bowl falsely claiming it had been made by Yu Shun. He obtained for a thousand gold pieces each the staff with which Duke Zhou had beaten Bo Qin, and the mat on which Confucius had sat at the Apricot Platform. With his funds exhausted, he then held in his left hand the bowl supposedly made by Yu Shun and in his right hand the staff of Duke Zhou, while wearing Confucius's mat around him, and went to beg in the marketplace, saying: "Please grant me even one coin from Tai Gong's Nine Treasuries."

stories.text: 千金子驕語人曰：「我富甚，汝何得不奉承？」貧者曰：「汝自多金子，我何與而奉汝耶？」富者曰：「倘分一半與汝何如？」答曰：「汝五百，我五百，我汝等耳，何奉焉？」又曰：「悉以相送，難道猶不奉我？」答曰：「汝失千金，而我得之，汝又當趨奉我矣。」
stories.translation: A man named Qian Jinzi, speaking haughtily to others, said: "I am very wealthy; how can you not flatter me?" The poor man replied: "You yourself are a rich man with much gold; why should I have anything to do with you and flatter you?" The wealthy man said, "What if I give half of it to you? How would that be?" He replied: "You have five hundred and I have five hundred; we are equal, so why should I flatter you?" The wealthy man said again: "If I give it all to you, would you still not flatter me?" He replied: "You have lost a thousand gold pieces and I have gained them; then you should be the one flattering me."

stories.text: 富翁謂貧人曰：「我家富十萬矣。」貧人曰：「我亦有十萬之蓄，何足為奇。」富翁驚問曰：「汝之十萬何在？」貧者曰：「你平素有了不肯用，我要用沒得用，與我何異？」
stories.translation: A wealthy man said to a poor person, "My family has become rich with 100,000 gold pieces." The poor man replied: "I also have a savings of 100,000; what is so remarkable about that?" The wealthy man was astonished and asked, "Where are your 100,00 debts?" The poor man said: "You usually have it but refuse to spend it; I want to use it but cannot. What is the difference between us?"

stories.text: 窮漢聞鄰家喊捉賊，忙將陽物插妻牝內。妻曰：「賊至有何高興？」答曰：「止此一物，藏好了，怕他怎麼？」
stories.translation: A poor man, hearing his neighbor shouting to catch a thief, hurriedly inserted his penis into his wife's vagina. His wife said: "What is there to be happy about when thieves are coming?" He replied: "There's only this one thing; if it's well hidden, what can they do about it?"

stories.text: 一窮人正在歡飲，或報以家中失火。其人即將衣帽一整，仍坐云：「不妨，家當盡在身上矣。」或曰：「令正卻如何？」答曰：「他怕沒人照管？」
stories.translation: A poor man was just enjoying a drink when someone reported that his home had caught fire. The man immediately straightened out his clothes and hat, and still sat there saying: "It's no problem; all my belongings are right on me." Someone asked: "What about your wife?" He replied: "Does he fear that no one will take care of her?"

stories.text: 暑月有擁夾被臥者，或問其故，答曰：「阿喲，綿被脫熱。」
stories.translation: In the hot summer months, there was someone lying in bed with a double quilt. When asked why, he replied: "Ah yo, the cotton quilt is too warm."

stories.text: 貧子持金銀錠行於街市，顧錠嘆曰：「若得你硬起來，我就好過日子了。」傍人待答曰：「要我硬卻不能夠，除非你硬了湊我。」
stories.translation: A poor man carried gold and silver ingots while walking in the marketplace. Looking at the ingots, he sighed and said: "If only you could become hard, I would be able to live well." A passerby replied: "I want to be hard but cannot; unless you become hard and come together with me."

stories.text: 客至乏人，大聲討茶，妻無奈，只得自送茶出。夫裝鼾摚●，乃大喝云：「你家男個那裡去了？」
stories.translation: When a guest arrived and there was no one to serve, he loudly demanded tea. His wife had no choice but to personally bring out the tea. The husband pretended to snore loudly, so she shouted: "Where is your family's man?"

stories.text: 一家客至，其夫喚茶不已。婦曰：「終年不買茶葉，茶從何來？」夫曰：「白滾水也罷。」妻曰：「柴沒一根，冷水怎得熱？」夫罵曰：「狗淫婦！難道枕頭裡就沒有幾根稻草？」妻回罵曰：「臭忘八！那些磚頭石塊，難道是燒得著的！」
stories.translation: When a guest came to his home, the husband kept calling for tea. His wife said: "We haven't bought any tea leaves all year; where would the tea come from?" The husband replied, "Then just boil some plain water." His wife said: "We don't even have a single stick of firewood; how can cold water be heated?" The husband scolded, "You shameless hussy!" "Is there not even a few stalks of rice straw in the pillow?" The wife retorted, "You stinking bastard!" "Are those bricks and stones supposed to be burnable?"

stories.text: 有留客吃茶者，苦無茶葉，往鄰家借之。久而不至，湯滾則溢，以冷水加之。既久，釜且滿矣，而茶葉終不得。妻謂夫曰：「茶是吃不成了，不如留他洗個浴罷。」
stories.translation: A man who wanted to offer tea to a guest found that he had no tea leaves and went to borrow some from his neighbor. After waiting for a long time without the neighbor returning, the boiling water overflowed, so he added cold water to it. After some time had passed and the pot was nearly full, he still could not obtain any tea leaves. His wife said to her husband: "We won't be able to serve the tea, so why not just let him take a bath instead?"

stories.text: 客至乏僕，暗借鄰家小廝掇茶。至客堂後，逡巡不前，其人厲聲曰：「為何不至？」僮曰：「我怕你家這隻凶狗。」
stories.translation: When a guest arrived and they lacked servants, the host secretly borrowed a neighbor's young servant to serve tea. After arriving at the guest hall, the boy hesitated and did not move forward, so the host shouted sternly: "Why have you not come?" The servant replied: "I am afraid of your fierce dog."

stories.text: 一人家貧，每日省米吃粥。怕人恥笑，囑子諱之，人前只說吃飯。一日，父同友人講話，等久不進，子往喚曰：「進來吃飯。」父曰：「今日手段快，緣何煮得恁早？」子曰：「早倒不早，今日又熬了些清湯。」
stories.translation: A man was poor and saved rice every day to make porridge. Afraid of being ridiculed by others, he instructed his son to keep it secret and only say they were eating rice when in front of people. One day, the father was talking with a friend and did not eat for a long time; his son went to call him saying: "Come in and have your meal." The father said, "Today the hands are fast—why was it cooked so early?" The son replied: "It's not particularly early; we also made some clear soup today."

stories.text: 一人鞋襪俱破，鞋歸咎於襪，襪又歸咎於鞋，交相訟之於官。官不能決，乃拘腳跟證之。腳跟曰：「小的一向逐出在外，何由得知？」
stories.translation: A man had both his shoes and socks in tatters. He blamed the shoes on the socks, while the socks in turn blamed the shoes; they quarreled with each other before an official. The official could not decide and thus summoned the heel as a witness. The heel said: "I have always been driven out and kept outside; how would I know anything?"

stories.text: 貧家蓋蒿薦，幼兒不知諱，父撻而戒之曰：「後有問者，但云蓋被。」一日父見客，而鬚上帶薦草，兒從後呼曰：「爹爹，且除去面上被屑著？」
stories.translation: A poor family used a mat made of wormwood as a bed covering. A young child did not know to be discreet, so the father beat him and warned: "If anyone asks later, just say it is a blanket." One day the father received guests and had wormwood grass on his beard. The child called from behind: "Father, shall I remove the blanket shavings from your face?"

stories.text: 一人家貧而不善飲，每出啖糟餅二枚，便有酣意。適遇友人問曰：「爾晨飲耶？」答曰：「非也，吃糟餅耳。」歸以語妻，妻曰：「呆子，便說吃酒，也妝些體面。」夫頷之。及出，仍遇此友，問如前，以吃酒對。友詰之：「酒熱吃乎？冷吃乎？」答曰：「是熯的。」友笑曰：「仍是糟餅。」既歸，而妻知之，咎曰：「汝如何說熯，須云熱飲。」夫曰：「我知道了。」再遇此友，不待問即誇云：「我今番的酒，是熱吃的！」友問曰：「你吃幾何？」其人伸手曰：「兩個。」
stories.translation: A poor man who was not good at drinking would, whenever he went out, eat two pieces of lees cake and immediately feel tipsy. One day when he met a friend, the friend asked: "Have you had your morning drink?" He replied: "No, I just ate some lees cakes." When he returned home and told his wife about it, she said: "Fool! You might as well say you had some wine; at least that would make us look a bit more presentable." The husband nodded in agreement. When he went out again, he met the same friend and was asked as before; this time he answered that he had been drinking wine. The friend questioned him: "Did you drink it hot?" Or cold?" He replied, "It was warmed up." The friend laughed and said: "It's still lees cake." After returning home, the wife found out and scolded him, saying: "How could you say it was warmed? You must have said it was hot." The husband replied: "I understand now." When he met this friend again, before being asked, he boasted: "This time I drank it hot!" The friend asked: "How much did you drink?" The man held up his hand and said, "Two."

stories.text: 清客見東翁燒黃熟香，輒掩鼻不聞，以其賤而不屑用也。主人曰：「黃熟雖不佳，還強似府上燒人言、木屑。」清客大詫曰：「我舍下何曾燒這兩件？」主人曰：「蚊煙是甚麼做的？」
stories.translation: A refined guest, seeing his host burning yellow ripe incense, would often cover his nose and pretend not to smell it, considering the incense cheap and unworthy of use. The host said: "Although yellow ripe incense is not good, it's still better than the gossip and sawdust you burn at your house." The refined guest was greatly surprised and said: "How could I ever burn those two things in my home?" The host replied, "What is mosquito coil smoke made of?"

stories.text: 有人拉友作會，友固拒之不得，乃曰：「汝若要我與會，除是跪我。」其人即下跪，乃許之。傍觀者曰：「些須會銀，左右要還他的，如此自屈，吾甚不取。」答曰：「我不折本的，他日討會錢，跪還我的日子正多哩。」
stories.translation: A man invited a friend to join an association. When the friend firmly refused but was unable to, he said: "If you want me to attend this meeting, then I must kneel before you." The man immediately knelt down, and the friend agreed. A bystander said: "This small amount of association money will eventually have to be paid back, one way or another. To humble yourself like this is something I strongly disapprove of." He replied: "I'm not losing anything. On the day I collect the association money, there will be many more days when they have to kneel and pay me back."

stories.text: 一人對客，忽轉身曰：「兄請坐，我去兌還一主會銀，就來奉陪。」才進即出，客問：「何不兌銀？」其人笑曰：「我曾算來，他是痴的，所以把會銀與我。我若還他，也是癡的了。」
stories.translation: A man was entertaining a guest when he suddenly turned and said: "Brother, please sit. I will go to redeem some association money now and return shortly to keep you company." He had just entered when he left again. The guest asked: "Why didn't you exchange the silver?" The man smiled and said, "I had calculated before; he is a fool, so he gave me the association money." "If I return it to him, I would also be a fool."

stories.text: 一窮人留客吃飯，其妻因飯少，以鵝卵石襯於添飯之下。及添飯既盡，而石出焉。主人見之愧甚，乃責僕曰：「瞎眼奴才，淘米的時節，眼睛生在那裡？這樣大石沙，都不拿來揀出。」
stories.translation: A poor man invited a guest to dinner. Because there was not enough rice, his wife placed some river pebbles underneath the added rice as padding. When all the extra rice had been eaten, the stones were revealed. The host was very ashamed and scolded his servant, saying: "Blind fool! Where were your eyes when you were washing the rice?" Such big stones of sand weren't even picked out."

stories.text: 一人不見了扇子，，罵曰：「拿我的扇子，去做羹飯！」傍人曰：「扇子如何做得羹飯？」其人曰：「你不曉得，我的扇子，糊掇許多飯粘在上面。」
stories.translation: A man who had lost his fan scolded, "Who took my fan and used it to make soup?" Someone nearby asked: "How can a fan be made into soup?" The man said, "You don't know—there is so much rice stuck to my fan."

stories.text: 窮人好妝體面，偶出訪友，乏人跟隨，令妻男妝以代僕。及至友家，閑談至暮，遂留宿焉。因鋪陳未備，主伴主，而僕伴僕，各睡一處。窮人解衣上床，下身無褲，次日起身後，主人嘆曰：「好笑這朋友，窮得褲子也無，只穿一件單布麻裙。」僕在傍曰：「這還算好，不像他管家，竟窮得屪子都精光。」
stories.translation: A poor man wanted to maintain a decent appearance. When he occasionally went out to visit friends and found no one to accompany him, he ordered his wife to dress up as a male servant in place of an actual attendant. When they arrived at the friend's home, they chatted idly until dusk and decided to stay overnight. As the accommodations were not fully prepared, the host slept with the guest, while the servant slept with the "servant," each in separate places. The poor man took off his clothes and got into bed, but found he had no pants on. The next morning after getting up, the host sighed and said: "How laughable this friend is—he's so poor that he doesn't even have pants to wear; he only wore a single piece of hemp skirt." The servant added from the side: "This is still better than his family—they are so poor that even their butts are bare."

stories.text: 一人衣多破孔，或戲之曰：「君衣好像棋盤，一路一路的。」其人笑曰：「不敢欺，再著著，還要打結哩。」
stories.translation: A man's clothes were full of holes. Someone teased him, saying: "Your clothes look like a chessboard, with row after row." The man laughed and said: "Don't be deceived. If I wear them some more, they will even need to be tied in knots."

stories.text: 有居服制而欲赴喜筵者，借得他人一羊皮襖，素冠而往。人知其有服也，因問：「尊服是何人的？」其人見友問及，以為譏誚其所穿之衣，乃遽視己身作色而言曰：「是我自家的，問他怎麼？」
stories.translation: A man, who was still in mourning but wanted to attend a wedding banquet, borrowed someone else's sheepskin coat and went there wearing his plain mourning cap. People knew he was in mourning and asked: "Whose mourning clothes are these?" Seeing his friend ask, the man thought he was being mocked for his clothes. He quickly looked at himself and said angrily: "These are my own clothes! What business is it of yours?"

stories.text: 一人三餐無食，夫妻枵腹上床。妻嗟嘆不已，夫曰：「我今夜連要打三個拐，以當三餐。」妻從之。次早起來，頭暈眼花，站腳不住，謂妻曰：「此事妙極，不惟可以當飯，且可當酒。」
stories.translation: A man had not eaten for three meals, and his husband and wife went to bed with empty stomachs. The wife sighed repeatedly, and the husband said: "Tonight I will have to turn over three times in bed, each one representing a meal." The wife followed suit. The next morning, after getting up, he felt dizzy and lightheaded, unable to stand steadily. He said to his wife: "This is wonderful! Not only can it substitute for food, but also for alcohol."

stories.text: 一窮人積米三四瓮，自謂極富。一日，與同伴行市中，聞路人語曰：「今歲收米不多，止得三千餘石。」窮人謂其伴曰：「你聽這人說謊，不信他一分人家，有這許多酒瓮。」
stories.translation: A poor man had stored three or four jars of rice and considered himself extremely wealthy. One day, while walking in the market with his companion, he overheard a passerby say: "This year's rice harvest is not great; we only got more than 3000 dan." The poor man said to his companion: "Listen to this man lying. I don't believe even one household has so many wine jars."

stories.text: 偷兒入貧家，遍摸無一物，乃唾地開門而去。貧者床上見之，喚曰：「賊，有慢了，可為我關好了門去。」偷兒曰：「你這樣人，虧你還叫我賊！我且問你，你的門關他做甚麼？」
stories.translation: A thief entered a poor household, searched everywhere but found nothing. He then spat on the ground, opened the door, and left. The poor man saw this from his bed and called out: "Thief, don't be so careless. Please close the door properly for me." The thief said: "You are such a person; it's a pity you still call me a thief!" "I'll ask you—what do you need your door closed for?"

stories.text: 穿窬入一貧家，其家止蓄米一瓮，置臥床前。偷兒解裙布地，方取瓮傾米，床上人竊窺之，潛抽其裙去，急呼「有賊」。賊應聲曰：「真個有賊，剛才一條裙在此，轉眼就被賊屄養的偷去了。」
stories.translation: A thief broke into a poor household. There was only one jar of rice stored in the house, placed before the bed. The thief took off his skirt and spread it on the floor to pour out the rice from the jar. The person in bed secretly pulled away the skirt, then shouted urgently: "There's a thief!" The thief responded: "Indeed there is a thief! Just now, I had one skirt here, and in the blink of an eye it was stolen by another thief's vagina."

stories.text: 穿窬往竊一家，見主人向外而睡，忽轉朝裡。賊疑其素有相識，欲遁去。其人大呼曰：「來不妨，因我家乏物可敬，無顏見你囉。」
stories.translation: A thief broke in to steal from a house and saw the homeowner sleeping with his back outward. Suddenly, the owner turned inward. The thief suspected that he might know this person and wanted to escape. The man shouted loudly: "Come in, there's no problem. Because my home has nothing worth offering, I'm too ashamed to see you."

stories.text: 貧士素好鋪張，偷兒夜襲之，空如也，唾罵而去。貧士摸床頭數錢，追贈之，囑曰：「君此來，雖極怠慢，然在人前尚望包荒。」
stories.translation: A poor scholar had always loved to appear extravagant. A thief attacked him at night but found the house empty, and he spat curses as he left. The poor scholar counted some money at the head of his bed, gave it to him as a gift in pursuit, and said: "Although I have been extremely rude this time, I still hope you will be kind enough to keep this matter private before others."

stories.text: 有持券借債者，主人曰：「券倒不須寫，只畫一幅行樂圖來。」借者問其故，答曰：「怕我日後討債時，便不是這副面孔耳。」
stories.translation: A man came to borrow money with a promissory note. The lender said: "The note is unnecessary; just draw me a picture of yourself having fun." The borrower asked why, and the lender replied: "I'm afraid that when I come to collect the debt later, you won't have this same cheerful face."

stories.text: 一貧人生前負債極多，死見冥王。王命鬼判查其履歷，乃慣賴人債者，來世罰去變成犬馬，以償前欠。貧者稟曰：「犬馬之報，所償有限，除非變了他們的親爺，方可還得。」王問何故，答曰：「做了他家的爺，盡力去掙，掙得論千論萬，少不得都是他們的。」
stories.translation: A poor man who had accumulated many debts in life appeared before the King of Hell after his death. The king ordered a ghost judge to check his record and found that he had been accustomed to defaulting on debts. As punishment, in the next life he would be transformed into a dog or horse to repay his past debts. The poor man pleaded: "Becoming a dog or horse can only repay part of the debt. Unless I am transformed into their own father, I will not be able to fully repay it." The King asked why, and he replied: "If I become their father, I can work hard to earn thousands or even ten thousand. Whatever I earn will inevitably belong to them."

stories.text: 欠債者謂討債者曰：「我命不久矣，昨夜夢見身死。」討者曰：「陰陽相反，夢死反得生也。」欠債者曰：「還有一夢。」問曰：「何夢？」曰：「夢見還了你的債。」
stories.translation: The debtor told the creditor: "My days are numbered. I dreamed last night that I had died." The creditor said: "Yin and Yang are opposite; dreaming of death means you will actually live." The debtor replied: "I had another dream." He asked, "What was the dream?" The debtor said: "I dreamed that I had repaid your debt."

stories.text: 一人為討債者所逼，乃發急曰：「你定要我說出來麼！」討債者疑其發己心病，嘿然而去。如此數次。一日發狠曰：「由你說出來也罷，我不怕你。」其人又曰：「真個要說出來？」曰：「真要你說。」曰：「不還了！」
stories.translation: A man, pressured by a creditor, suddenly exclaimed in desperation: "You really want me to say it out loud?!" The creditor suspected he was trying to provoke his emotions and silently left. This happened several times. One day, the creditor said angrily: "Go ahead and say it out loud if you want; I'm not afraid of you." The man replied: "You really want me to say something?" He said, "Yes, I do." The man said: "I won't repay it!"

stories.text: 一家索債人多，椅凳俱坐滿，更有坐檻上者。主人私謂坐檻者云：「足下明日來早些。」那人意其先完己事，乃大喜，遂揚言以散眾人。次早黎明即往，叩其相約之意。答曰：「昨日有褻坐檻，甚是不安，今日早來，可佔把交椅。」
stories.translation: A house was filled with creditors collecting debts; all the chairs and benches were occupied, and some even sat on the window sills. The homeowner privately told the one sitting on the sill: "Please come a little earlier tomorrow." Thinking that he would be settled first, the man was overjoyed and loudly announced to disperse the crowd. The next morning at dawn, he went there immediately to inquire about their previous arrangement. He replied: "Yesterday you sat on the sill in an indecent manner, which made me very uncomfortable. Coming early today will allow you to occupy a proper chair."

stories.text: 有欠債屢索不還者，主人怒，命僕輩潛伺其出，扛之以歸。至中途，僕暫歇息，其人曰：「快走罷，歇在這裡，又被別人扛去，不關我事。」
stories.translation: There was a debtor who had been repeatedly asked to repay the debt but refused. The creditor became angry and ordered his servants to secretly wait for him outside, then carry him back. Halfway through the journey, the servants paused to rest. The debtor said: "Hurry up and walk! If we stop here, someone else might carry me away, which would have nothing to do with me."

stories.text: 冥王命拘蔡青，鬼卒誤聽，以為勾債精也，遂攝一欠債者到案。王詢之，知其謬，命鬼卒放回。債精曰：「其實不願回去。陽間無處藏身，正要借此處一躲。」
stories.translation: The King of Hell ordered the arrest of Cai Qing. The ghost soldiers misunderstood and thought it meant capturing a debt collector, so they brought in a debtor instead. The King questioned him and realized the mistake, then ordered the ghost soldiers to release him. The debt collector said: "Actually, I don't want to go back." There is nowhere for me to hide in the mortal world. I was just hoping to take refuge here for a while."

stories.text: 一人專好放生，龍王感之，命夜叉贈一寶錢，囑曰：「此錢名為擺海乾，教他把此錢在海中一擺，海水即乾，任將金銀寶貝拿去。」夜叉使命付訖。其人日日將錢去擺，遂成大富。後把此錢失去，貪心未足，只將空手海上去擺。一日，撞著夜叉，夜又曰：「你手內錢都沒了，還有何臉面，在此擺甚麼？」
stories.translation: A man was particularly fond of releasing animals back into the wild. The Dragon King, moved by this, ordered a night demon to give him a treasure coin and instructed: "This coin is called Bai Haiqian. Tell him to wave it once in the sea, and the seawater will dry up, allowing him to take as much gold, silver, and treasures as he wants." The night demon completed his mission. Every day, the man waved the coin, and thus became very wealthy. Later, when he lost this coin, his greed was still unsatisfied, so he went to the sea with empty hands and waved them. One day, he bumped into a night demon who said: "The money in your hands is already gone. What face do you have to wave around here?"
